body.purpose: Forms, registers, labels, and audit detail.

shadows.name: approval-dock
shadows.purpose: Keeps the final review control visually anchored.

narrative.overview: Ledgerly feels like a composed set of working papers rather than a generic software dashboard. Warm paper, an ink-dark docket rail, audit-gold details, and precise approval and exception colors make every screen feel accountable, calm, and ready for scrutiny.
keyCharacteristics: Evidence and status stay visually adjacent.
Registers and ruled lists carry operational information.
Every simulated action is visibly labeled.

rules.name: The Control Color Rule
rules.body: Approval teal and exception vermilion communicate state; they are never ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Working-Paper Rule
rules.body: Elevation marks a movable or decision-bearing sheet, never a decorative tile.

dos: Do keep source evidence, proposed accounting treatment, and review action in one visible workflow.
Do preserve client scope and exception context at every breakpoint.
donts: Don't use approval or exception colors for decoration.
Don't introduce generic equal-card metric grids or unlabeled mock operations.
